# We Won’t Let Them Get Away With It.
The executive branch is corrupt and overpowered. The Epstein Class goes unpunished, and AI could cause chaos if we don’t have a thoughtful plan. Jamie is the 100% grassroots underdog candidate, living in Berkeley, with both the relevant expertise and the plan we need to meet this political moment. Vote for integrity this election!
#### Jamie Joyce is also your only congressional candidate who:
✔️ Has never taken Corporate PAC money (read more)
✔️ Has never taken Pro-Israel PAC money (read more)
✔️ Has a plan for the district, AI, surveillance, ICE, and to fight the Epstein Class (read more below)
✔️ Has the professional background to address the biggest challenges that lay ahead!
Donate to Jamie's Campaign

## Why Jamie Joyce & Why Now
Hey neighbors! We are entering a new territory of politics and of technology. We won’t have many chances to get this right, and we don’t have time for Congress to play catch-up. I happen to be a multidisciplinary expert who has has spent my life dedicated to research, democracy-tech, and charity, and I believe I have exactly the right expertise we need to meet the moment, including:
#### Having A Plan for AI (click here)
7 in 10 Americans say the federal government isn't doing enough to regulate AI. Part of the problem is that many members of Congress don't understand the technology, and you can't govern well what you don't understand.
I do. I've spent years in the AI field, leading projects in autonomous research, fact-checking agents, and AI-powered formal reasoning for evidence-based policy. OpenAI and xAI have invited me to present my work internally. Anthropic researchers have mentioned it in published research on AI and democracy. I'm endorsed by Tristan Harris, one of the world's best-known AI ethicists. My work in AI is respected across the aisle, though no, large AI labs are not funding my campaign, but the current corporate Democrat’s plan is to put AI SuperPAC funded candidates in charge of AI in the new Congress. To me, that is not acceptable. We need people in Congress who will fight for people, not corporations, and this district has the chance to send someone with a proven track record of doing this. See more detail about my work in AI here.
That's why I wrote the AI section of the MAD Act: 240+ pages of serious policy. It includes immediate red-line regulations, interim safeguards, and hammer provisions. It also requires the government to build a real, evidence-based plan for AI's impact across 19 domains, from jobs to the environment.
AI is a powerful tool, and people should be allowed to keep building with it to make new discoveries and improve services. But we need guardrails that make sure it works for people, children, the environment, and the economy, not against them. America doesn't need another campaign promise. It needs a plan for AI that actually works, and I've already written one. So I hope you send me to Congress to keep advocating for policy that works - especially as the technology and industry keep rapidly evolving.
#### Holding the Epstein Class Accountable (click here)
If you care about this issue, you are not alone. 84% of voters, across party lines, want accountability on the Epstein Files. And Congress isn't delivering it.
Epstein partied with princes, prime ministers, and presidents - including at least two of our own. This is why this case matters to everyone, and not just survivors: many of those same powerful people write the rules the rest of us live by. This case is one of our best chances at exposing the transnational network of criminals who coordinate with the heads of governments all over the world. Because our own government may be implicated, we may be a nation under the most despicable kind of blackmail. So it's time to take power out of the Epstein Class’s hands - and I intend to.
How? Uniquely, I've actually worked in the government files field, so I noticed a few gaps when Congress passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act. The bill Congress drafted never asked for files from agencies like the Treasury, the IRS, and the intelligence agencies. This would be an easier way to see who is in the network - by identifying who was paying Epstein and who Epstein was paying. Worse, a drafting issue exposed survivors' identities, harming the very people the law was supposed to protect. Instead of owning the error, Congress continues to blame the DOJ for what Congress made permissible. It was actually this work pointing out these failures that earned me the endorsement of Epstein survivors, because this should have never happened and we cannot keep tolerating these kinds of oversights. Law deserves meticulous attention. We cannot drop this case. We cannot let them get away with it.
To fix Congress’ oversights, I went ahead and drafted legislation to close those gaps and sent it to every Senate and House office, including Ro Khanna's. (Read more about it.) We need to protect survivors, root out the rot in our own government, and bring justice to anyone who is complicit in this multi-decade, transnational crime.
#### Reining in ICE, Surveillance, Dark Money & More (click here)
There are several urgent threats to our democratic system, this includes the overreach of ICE, the expanding surveillance state, and dark money flooding our elections, amidst other issues. As soon as I filed to run in the primary election, I sat down and spent hundreds of hours researching how to address these issues and put solutions into draft legislation. Similar to the topic of the Epstein files, my team then began emailing congressional offices across the country and taking meetings with legislative staff after the incumbent Congresswoman refused to meet me personally.
If you would like to read about this draft legislation, you can find the text below:
Delete the surveillance state (read more)
Get ICE off our streets (read more)
Shine a light on dark money (read more)
Enable election reform (read more)
And more (Read MAD Act Website and Full Bill Text / Other Titles)
However, I have also worked in the climate/ environmental sector, the humanitarian/ sustainable development sector, and the civic tech sector - including teaching students from 30 Universities how to analyze legislation. I am committed to learning what I need to be able to legislate and vote well on the issues this country, and district, will face. To learn more about what I am tracking for the district, see the section at the bottom of this website. To learn more about my background, my community work, my humanitarian work, and professional associations which I believe equip me to be a well-rounded representative, see here.
To read more about Jamie’s background, click here. To read Jamie’s fact-check of incumbent Rep. Simon’s claims about her bringing a billion dollars to the district, click here (hint: doesn’t look true).
## So What’s Jamie’s Plan?
If elected, I’m arriving with a legislative plan in hand, a strategy to make Congress act on it, and a long-term vision for a modern Congress that answers to everyday people (not special interests) - all the while serving District 12.
My legislation, “The MAD Act,” addresses the critical, triage items including reining in AI, ICE, surveillance, getting more Epstein Files, shining a light on dark money, funding electoral reform, etc. (which can be individual titles, and not an omnibus) so Congress can be reliably responsive in delivering other policies we want, like: healthy food, a clean environment, fair taxes, affordable living, housing, and healthcare, as well as ending war/genocide. Every common sense policy is downstream of a government that actually works for us - so addressing the corruption and unresponsiveness in government is where we need to start. Here are the plans:
#### First, Serving District 12 (click here)
A representative can’t be in every place at once, but issues across the district need attention and constituents already bring up these issues across various platforms, including: letters to the editor, in council meetings, and online. Instead of waiting for the issues to come to me, I built a tool to monitor conversations online and collect issues which voters are publicly discussing and want addressed. This can be used to inform project appropriations and efforts to finally resolve longstanding issues.
If you would like to review what we are tracking as needed throughout the district, you can find more information here.
- You can visit each city directory below. Please tell me if you see a missing need, and we will add it to our list.
Information on Berkeley
Information on Oakland
Information on Piedmont
Information on Albany
Information on Alameda
Information on Emeryville
Information on San Leandro
#### The "MAD Act" Legislation to Fix Federal Issues (click here)
We face immense power assymetries. Our government was designed to exist in a balance, but our government (and the executive branch in particular) has in their possession the most sophisticated intelligence, surveillance, secrecy, weapons, and military might. People are simple outmatched. We need to balance these powers between the branches, and also rebalance power between the people and government itself. So after Jamie announced she was running for office as a democratic candidate, she spent several hundred hours writing The MAD Act (The Mass Accountability in Democracy Act). The MAD Act is a 750 page omnibus bill that rebalances power between government and the people. It takes aim at the tools that the Epstein class has at their disposal to maintain power and ensures our democracy is prepared for AI impact.
There is a lot we need to fix:
Make a plan for AI: we can keep the benefits, and stop the harms (read more)
Delete the surveillance state (read more)
Get more Epstein files from the 70+ entities we missed the first time (read more)
Get ICE off our streets (read more)
Shine a light on dark money (read more)
Enable election reform (read more)
And more (Read MAD Act Website and Full Bill Text / Other Titles)
This bill does not need to be an omnibus, but each of these power asymmetries needs to be addressed. Introducing each title individually is fine, as long as we get dark money out of our elections, fund electoral reform, delete the surveillance state, reign in ICE, etc., in turn.
The MAD Act is not “anti-AI,” “anti-security,” “anti-business,” or “anti-government,” it is simply pro-responsibility, safety, accountability, and aggressively defends our rights.
Jamie has been meeting with members of Congress across the country to build allies to introduce and pass either the individual titles or the full MAD Act.
#### Strategy to Force Congressional Action (click here)
The “Just 12” Strategy
Jamie is ready to serve as a legislator, but if elected, she's just 1 of 435. She's running as a Democrat, but she refuses to let a "blue wave" become “business as usual.” She's been that disappointed voter too many times.
So she has a strategy: build a disruptive voting bloc.
Jamie is recruiting 11 other congressional candidates from across the political spectrum to run as a unified bloc. Why 12 in total? Because neither party can pass legislation in the House without a majority. Twelve members who refuse to rubber-stamp bills that don't serve the people become a critical voting unit if the house is full - which is likely with the most contentious issues.
Both republicans and democrats answer to special interests. A Democratic majority alone won't guarantee the progress we need. But 12 united members who answer only to voters can help change the game.
This voting bloc doesn’t need to outnumber anyone, they just need to ensure that every bill to earn their vote by truly representing public interest.
That's not intending to be disruptive for the sake of disruption. This is leverage. And that's how the game changes. Congress can either come to the table and negotiate or things grind to a halt and the public will become more and more aware of the common-sense, bipartisan demands being made that people across the spectrum agree needs to happen - like getting dark money out of our elections.
#### Efforts to Modernize Congress (click here)
Congress is an antique institution in the 21st century. It was devised when sending a message required delivering paper on horseback - though now we bounce signals off of satellites in space to talk to people around the world.
If elected, Jamie aims to map the workflows of Congress and bring technology into offices to ensure staff are able to be more accountable, effective, and transparent in their work for both the American people and their districts. It can start with small updates - like allowing the constituents of District 12 to text Jamie’s office instead of needing to call in order to report their concerns.
But the overall goal is to bring more transparency and access for constituents. Congress is needlessly a black box. But what’s currently done in the dark can be brought to light - to the benefit of everyone.
## Why Not the Incumbent, Lateefah Simon?
Here are the biggest wedge issues:
☑️ Evidence suggests she is being dishonest about her record by claiming she delivered “hundreds of millions” or “over a billion” to the district
☑️ She has taken corporate PAC money, Pro-Israel PAC money and endorsement (prioritizing the interests of corporations and other nations is a conflict of interest at best).
☑️ It seems she won’t fight the party because she wants to advance her career by getting committee assignments (like the appropriations committee), and we can’t let a “blue wave” become “business as usual.”
☑️ We need public servants in office who understand AI and technology so they can legislate effectively, it’s simply time to pass the torch!
Note: Jamie supports Israel’s right to exist, but not its interest in colonizing Gaza, which is currently suffering from a genocidal campaign that must be stopped immediately. Block the bombs, bring in the humanitarian aide, and end the famine.

# Professional Endorsements
Unlike traditional political endorsements, among Jamie’s early endorsers represent locally-based, world-recognized leaders who have been on the forefront of fighting for humanity’s future.
Together, they provide testimony to Jamie’s expertise in tech, AI, ethics, knowledge access, and an understanding of complex systems, as well as her love of the environment and growing human-centered cultural movements here in this district as well as around the world. To see reviews of Jamie’s leadership, see here.

# Jamie Speaks In D.C.; Endorsed by Epstein Survivors
Jun 29
Written By Jamie Joyce
Congressional candidate Jamie Joyce presents draft legislation to fix three flaws in the Epstein Files Transparency Act
Proposal would protect survivors, broaden records requests beyond the DOJ, and use Congress's own power to declassify, with backing from three Epstein survivors.
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Jamie Joyce, candidate for California's 12th Congressional District, was endorsed by three Epstein Survivors after she released draft legislation to repair three critical flaws in the original Epstein Files Transparency Act - a part of her omnibus bill “The MAD Act.” These are gaps that, Jamie argued, caused the law to expose survivors instead of revealing Jeffrey Epstein's network. Speaking at the Donald J. Trump and Epstein Files Reading Room in D.C., Jamie Joyce urged Congress to pass a stronger bill and offered her own draft for the taking.
During the 30 minute technical talk, she broke down exactly how the current law has produced roughly 3.5 million heavily redacted pages, but few true answers. Even with Katie Phang’s recent victory in court asking for redactions to be removed and for survivors to be protected, there are still more files to seek out.
Jamie explained that the original Epstein Files Transparency Act fell short in three ways:
A single word that failed survivors. The Act said the Attorney General "shall" release the files but only "may" redact survivors' personally identifiable information, including medical records. This effectively made survivor protection optional. Survivors' names, addresses, and former workplaces were therefore released publicly. However, her new draft makes those redactions mandatory.
Records from only one agency. Congress requested files solely from the Department of Justice. The draft directs requests to dozens of additional sources, including intelligence agencies, financial and tax regulators, and the National Archives. The MAD Act would also compel specific record types to be turned over, such as IRS reviews, FinCEN Suspicious Activity Reports, and federal visitor logs.
An unused path to declassification. The original bill released only "unclassified" material. The new draft invokes Congress's own authority to override executive classification which is maintained through court interpretation of the classification rights of the executive branch. This is the principle which courts have affirmed in the Nixon tapes case, when the public's right to know outweighed the executive's claim to secrecy.
#### "It was a one difference - it could have been “shall,” it could have been “must,” but it was a one word difference that failed to protect survivors’ personally identifiable information."— Jamie Joyce
Every single member of Congress except for one voted for this, when they could have made even just a one-word amendment to protect survivors. Jamie discussed the proposal with survivors at the Reading Room, three of whom present voiced support and officially endorsed her candidacy. When asked about why the Epstein Files were such an important issue to advance in her campaign, Jamie argues that the potential implication of the President himself, his administration, and other government representatives across administrations points to the corrupt coverup of our own military-intelligence and executive branch’s negligence on the rampant abuse of women and children.
#### “We must investigate the Epstein case to the maximal extent,” says Joyce, “because it may reveal that we are not actually a sovereign nation after all, but instead operating under blackmail that’s potentially held by a foreign nation which was originally created by Epstein. It is a thread worth pulling on until we reveal the truth about whether there is a web of influence that is preventing our government from serving the United States’ peoples interests. If our government is, in any way, implicated in the horrific abuse of Epstein, the American people demand to know and they demand justice.”
A part of Jamie’s argument for her candidacy is that the fact this bill passed without any amendments that would have protected survivors and surfaced more files is evidence that the people should elect representatives who have expertise - and pay attention to details. Jamie Joyce is making the full legislative draft available to any member of Congress or candidate who wishes to introduce it as a separate title: Title VII. Watch the full presentation below.
